title: The Syringe Changes Its Place in the Sentence
subtitle: A dated reading of how policy language moves between service, danger, and public explanation

events.title: Martial Law Begins in Taiwan Province
events.summary: Taiwan and Penghu remained under prolonged martial law until 1987; the dates when it ended in different territories must be distinguished.

events.title: Martial Law Ends in Taiwan and Penghu
events.summary: Martial law ended in Taiwan and Penghu on July 15, 1987.
events.analysis: Institutional change and changes in everyday treatment can be compared; the date alone does not establish changes in school culture or policing.

events.title: The Changde Street Police Check Controversy
events.summary: Dozens were taken to a police station between late on July 30 and early on July 31; participants’ accounts differ from those of the police.

events.title: The Yeh Yung-chih Case
events.summary: Found seriously injured in a school restroom, he died the next day. A history of bullying over gender expression is not proof that he was beaten to death.

events.title: Heping Hospital Locked Down During SARS
events.summary: Taiwan CDC records the Heping Hospital lockdown during the 2003 SARS outbreak.
events.analysis: The essay places hospital infection and coordination problems beside subsequent institutional reforms; this selected chronology is not a full causal account.

events.title: The First Taiwan Pride Parade
events.summary: The Taiwan Pride organizer dates the first parade to November 1, 2003.
events.analysis: The essay reads public visibility beside later civic organizing; this single date does not measure social recognition.

events.title: The Nong’an Street Police Operation
events.summary: More than 90 people were taken to a police station, prompting concerns about privacy and HIV stigma; sources give differing totals of 92 and 93.

events.title: Gender Equity Education Act Enacted
events.summary: The original law explicitly covered gender characteristics and sexual orientation; gender identity and gender-based bullying were expressly included in later amendments.

events.title: National Health Command Center Opens
events.summary: A permanent foundation for preparedness, distinct from command centers activated for specific outbreaks.

events.title: Harm Reduction Pilot Launched
events.summary: Official accounts date the launch to August, in response to the HIV epidemic among people who inject drugs.

events.title: The Honeymoon Bay Attack
events.summary: A near-contemporaneous Judicial Reform Foundation account describes gay men being attacked for kissing and questions whether police protection was adequate.

events.title: Methadone Maintenance Treatment Introduced
events.summary: Expanded nationwide in June of the same year; oral substitution treatment is distinct from needle services.

events.title: H1N1 Command Center Established
events.summary: The cited CDC record dates establishment of the H1N1 command center to April 28, 2009.

events.title: Puma Shen Publishes an Essay on Drug Policy
events.summary: Discusses punishment, decriminalization, social work, and harm reduction; its scope is not explicitly limited to methadone.

events.title: Street Mobilization for Marriage Equality
events.summary: A Ketagalan Boulevard concert and cross-party lobbying accompanied the Equality Bees’ expansion of everyday public outreach.

events.title: Judicial Yuan Interpretation No. 748
events.summary: Affirms constitutional guarantees of freedom to marry and equality, requiring legislation within two years.

events.title: Referendums on Marriage and LGBTQ Education
events.summary: The results of different proposals shaped the legislative route but did not overturn constitutional protections.

events.title: “Womxnly” Released
events.summary: Included on Ugly Beauty, the song pays particular tribute to Yeh Yung-chih while addressing a broader range of experiences of difference.

events.title: Special Same-Sex Marriage Legislation Takes Effect
events.summary: Passed its third reading on May 17 and took effect on May 24; reforms on transnational marriage and adoption followed.

events.title: COVID-19 Command Center Established
events.summary: Taiwan CDC records establishment of the COVID-19 command center on January 20, 2020.
events.analysis: The essay places this coordination record beside later public instruction; it does not measure individual knowledge or explain the 2026 response.

events.title: Public Guidance on Home Rapid Tests
events.summary: Explains how to use tests and respond to results, with a reminder that a negative result does not remove the need for precautions.

events.title: Home Care Guidelines for People with COVID-19
events.summary: Guidance on reporting and monitoring symptoms and recognizing warning signs that require medical attention.

events.title: Adoption Rights Expanded for Same-Sex Spouses
events.summary: Rights including joint adoption continued to expand, while remaining subject to assessment and court approval.

events.title: Controversy over a Harvard Speech Photograph
events.summary: The contemporaneous report records Chiang at the Tianmu event and the deputy mayor and department heads at Pride. The later city-government account adds a claim that Chiang attended both. These accounts do not, by themselves, settle his full itinerary or identify the setting and date of each photograph.

sources.title: Contemporaneous 2023 report: Chiang attends the Tianmu event; deputy mayor and others attend Pride
The city government’s later account in 2026: claims attendance at both events

events.title: Harm Reduction Becomes an Electoral Dispute
events.summary: CNA reports the October 3 exchange over passages from Shen’s 2014 essay and proposed community drug-policy measures.
events.analysis: Selected quotations, community needle services, and methadone require separate policy distinctions.

events.title: Controversy over the Commander D Search
events.summary: Police say they had a search warrant; customers and lawyers question the legal basis for taking people to the station as a group and how they were treated. In September, the mayor had instructed police to investigate after a city councilor raised the issue. The specific decisions to search the venue and take customers to the station, along with the procedures applied to each person, remain to be established.

sources.title: Police account and the September administrative context

events.title: Media Report More Than 300,000 Comments
events.summary: The cited media report records more than 300,000 comments at a particular moment.
events.caveat: An attributed media count, not independently reverified platform data, distinct people, a live API reading, or a representative opinion poll.

events.title: Council Questioning and an Administrative Directive
events.summary: The contemporaneous report records Hung Chien-yi presenting a parent’s complaint and venue photographs in council, Chiang calling for inspections and strict enforcement, and the venue denying that it arranged the alleged conduct while saying it checked customers’ identities and ages.
events.caveat: The complaint is an allegation. This record does not establish minors’ involvement or the specific methods and authorization of the later search.

sources.title: Contemporaneous council report and venue response

events.title: Chiang Clarifies Support for Existing Harm Reduction
events.summary: NOWnews reports Chiang expressing support for methadone and needle and syringe policies while distinguishing those services from the community drug-supply proposal discussed in the older essay.
events.caveat: An attributed statement, not evidence of a policy change or measured audience response. Exact publication time was not independently reverified in this revision pass.

cutoffScope: Editorial selection boundary; not a claim of exhaustive collection or independently reverified publication timestamps
